svg.title: VarMQ worker pool with concurrency 4
svg.desc: The queue starts empty and the pool holds a single idle worker goroutine; concurrency 4 is only the upper limit. Add is called six times in a row. Each call tries to signal the event loop, but the signal channel holds only one pending signal, so the other five are dropped. From that one signal the event loop dispatches four jobs back to back: the first goes to Worker 1 and Workers 2, 3 and 4 are spawned for the next three, until every slot is busy; the remaining two jobs wait in the queue. When a worker finishes and no other worker is idle, it stays in the pool and receives the next job; when another worker is already idle, it exits. As the queue drains, the pool shrinks back to the single idle Worker 1 and the event loop waits.
